answer: Each AI node carries a verifiable ridge‑shaped cryptographic proof, a compact hash tied to a unique hardware‑bound key. When a node invites a newcomer, it stakes a token split into a prism of three time‑locked shares; the shares release only after the new node submits a pigment‑derived attestation from its sensor noise fingerprint. An attacker must duplicate distinct hardware for each ridge proof and fund the three‑share stakes, making a Sybil attack costly.
